# Valgrind shard scope — which `alkahest-cas` unit tests the nightly
# `valgrind` and `valgrind-validated` shards run under memcheck.
#
# Read by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, step "Valgrind — Rust/C FFI boundary".
#
# Format, one entry per line:   <shard>   filter|skip   <libtest substring>
#
#   filter  — passed to the test binary as a positional filter (substring
#             match, not a regex; several filters are OR-ed).
#   skip    — passed as `--skip` (substring match), and removes the tests it
#             matches from whatever the filters selected.
#
# Before valgrind starts, the step lists the binary's tests (no valgrind, so
# instantly) and fails if any filter *or* skip matches zero tests: a renamed
# test cannot turn a filter into a vacuous pass or a skip into dead text. It
# then prints how many tests the shard will run, and after the run fails if
# memcheck executed none.
#
# Every skip says why, and what does check that code instead. TESTING.md §3
# ("Valgrind") lists the same coverage for readers who do not open this file.
#
# Wall-clock bounds: the step sets ALKAHEST_TEST_TIME_SCALE=50 (memcheck is a
# 20–50× slowdown), which `test_time::limit` multiplies every scaled test
# deadline and budget by. A test with a fixed `Duration` bound fails under
# valgrind for no memory reason — use `crate::test_time::limit*` instead of
# adding a skip here.

# ── valgrind: the GMP / MPFR / FLINT boundary ──────────────────────────────
# The tests whose code crosses into C: ball arithmetic (Arb), anything named
# for FLINT or rug, number theory and lattices (all bignum), and the binomial
# factoriser's FLINT comparisons on small inputs.
valgrind            filter  ball::
valgrind            filter  flint
valgrind            filter  rug
valgrind            filter  number_theory::
valgrind            filter  lattice::
valgrind            filter  poly::factor::binomial::

# These three run FLINT's Zassenhaus / van Hoeij factoriser on dense
# polynomials of degree up to 300 (`x^n ± 1` for every n ≤ 300; degree-240
# `x^n − 1` products), which is seconds natively and did not finish in five
# hours under memcheck: from the nightly of 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-07 they were
# the only tests still running when the job hit GitHub's 6 h cap, every
# night, and the shard was cancelled with its result unreported. The same
# FFI entry points (`fmpz_poly_factor`, the coefficient round trip) are
# exercised here on small inputs by the rest of `poly::factor::binomial::`
# and by the `flint` filter (`flint_builder_matches_coeffmap`,
# `flint_mul_matches_schoolbook`, …); the three tests in full run under ASan
# (memory errors) and LSan (leaks) in the `asan` and `lsan` shards.
valgrind            skip    poly::factor::binomial::tests::x_n_pm_1_matches_flint
valgrind            skip    poly::factor::binomial::tests::scaled_and_shifted_binomials_match_flint
valgrind            skip    poly::factor::tests::canonical_order_is_independent_of_flint

# ── valgrind-validated: rigorous enclosures over Arb ───────────────────────
valgrind-validated  filter  validated::
# `validated::bounds::` does not finish under memcheck at all: the nightly of
# 2026-10-05 spent 4 h inside it and was cancelled at the 6 h cap with most of
# its 55 tests unrun. They are enclosure searches over the same Arb calls the
# rest of `validated::` makes; ASan and LSan run them in full.
valgrind-validated  skip    validated::bounds::
